text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Austrian newspapers:

- Finance Minister Viktor Klima will have to choose the highest bid of the three offers for the government's 70 percent stake in flagship bank Creditanstalt, according to European Union regulations. The surprise third offer came from former retail chain owner Karl Wlaschek, who had sold his chain only this year.
- The atmosphere in the coalition government remains frosty over the issue of the privatisation of Creditanstalt.
- Austria's inflation rate rose to 2.3 percent in November from 2.1 percent in October.
- Turnover of luxury hosiery maker Wolford climbed by 64.6 million schillings to 829.3 million in the first half.
- Sales of motorbikes in Austria went up ten percent in 1996, despite bad weather this year.

- Klima intends to decide before the end of the year which of the bidders for Creditanstalt - either Karl Wlaschek, Bank Austria or the consortium around insurer EA-Generali - will receive the government's stake in the bank.
- According to official studies, the number of people seeking an apprenticeship will grow in 1997 as the number of available places shrinks.
- Austria is number 18 out of 150 countries in an index of "economic freedom", a study by a U.S. conservative thinktank shows.

- Klima says the tax-payer is the only sure winner in the sale of Creditanstalt. If Bank Austria's bid is successful, the privatisation of the government's stake in Bank Austria will be easier. The newspaper believes Karl Wlaschek has offered 13 billion schillings, the consortium around EA-Generali altogether 14 billion schillings and Bank Austria nearly 17 billion schillings.
- Post & Telekom Austria will take on 66 billion schillings of old debts from Austria's postal service. However, PTA is due to receive income from the privatisation of the postal saving's bank PSK.
- The ATX index of 21 blue chips climbed 16 points after the bids for Creditanstalt were made public on Monday.
- Skimaker Fischer's hi-tech unit Fischer Advanced Composite Components has received orders from Boeing and Airbus supplier Alenia worth 400 million schillings and 20 million schillings respectively.
